title: Macbeth Themes: Application Adventure
welcome_lead: Apply your knowledge to imagery patterns - blood, sleep, light, dark, and the natural order undone.
meta_desc: Application practice on Macbeth's motifs of blood, sleep, light and disorder.
final_note: You can now connect motif to theme. Stretch with full context next.

concepts.def: Marks guilt that cannot be washed off.
Lost sleep stands for lost innocence.
Darkness hides crimes; dawn returns with Malcolm.
Witches' double meanings trick Macbeth into confidence.
Storms and horses eating each other mark unnatural acts.
Macbeth murders his way through suspicion to oppression.

walkthroughs.body_html: Macbeth asks if 'all great Neptune's ocean' will wash his hand clean and decides his blood would rather 'the multitudinous seas incarnadine'. Lady Macbeth dismisses it: 'A little water clears us of this deed.' By Act 5 she has reversed: 'Will these hands ne'er be clean?' The motif tracks moral knowledge.

Lady Macbeth calls on 'thick night' to hide her knife; Macbeth begs 'stars, hide your fires'. Each murder happens in literal or symbolic darkness. When Malcolm marches with Birnam Wood the daylight returns - moral order is restored with the rightful king.

Old Man and Ross note Duncan's horses 'eat each other' and an owl killed a falcon. Shakespeare uses the medieval Great Chain of Being: regicide breaks nature itself. Disorder in the cosmos mirrors disorder in the kingdom.
